implemented.text: Every signal comes from a public source on the open web and carries a dated link. All content was produced and frozen offline before release, every shipped item passed verification, and the published files are regenerated byte for byte from that frozen output.

Nothing you type is stored or sent. The demo uses no browser storage and no cookies, puts none of your text in the address bar and makes no network requests, so your gut readings and rationales exist only in this tab and are gone when you close it.
No AI service is called while you use the demo. Every AI-generated text was written offline before release and ships inside the demo's own files, and the page makes no network requests.
There are no accounts, no cookies and no analytics. The page loads no remote script, font or image, contacts no server, and sets no cookie.

notImplemented.text: Ingestion of a team's own data is not implemented. It is argued below and not built, pending verified GDPR and EU compliance: the page makes no network requests and reads only the content frozen into this build.
Judgements are not kept across sessions. The demo writes nothing to browser storage, so closing or reloading the tab discards them.
The role-aware data model for a team of several founders (R7) is designed in the architecture and not built: no content carries a role, and no page code reads one.

argument.text: If own-data ingestion used AI to analyse the team, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, the AI Act, would also bear on it. The European Commission states that the Act became applicable on 2 August 2026, that its prohibitions, including emotion recognition in workplaces, have applied since February 2025, and that AI tools for employment and the management of workers are high-risk. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, the Digital Omnibus on AI, is adopted law: it entered into force on 27 July 2026 and amends the AI Act, including the dates from which its high-risk rules apply. According to the Commission, those obligations start on 2 December 2027 for the listed areas and on 2 August 2028 for AI embedded in products. Whether a feature that reads a founding team's judgements falls within the employment category is a condition to settle before it is built, and this demo does not settle it.

argument.text: These conditions rest on the GDPR's definition of personal data as it stands. The Commission's Digital Omnibus proposal COM(2025) 837 of 19 November 2025 would amend the GDPR, including that definition; the European Parliament's Legislative Train, updated on 20 September 2026, lists it as tabled, so it is a proposal and not law. In a joint opinion on the proposal, the European Data Protection Board and the European Data Protection Supervisor supported several GDPR simplifications but opposed the change to the definition of personal data as significantly narrowing it. A build of own-data ingestion would therefore be assessed against the GDPR in force when it is built, not against the proposal.
